title: Empty a urinary drainage bag into a graduate without the tube touching it, then close the valve and sleeve the spout
instruction: Empty the drainage bag into the graduate without letting the drain tube or its spout touch the graduate, then close the drain and push the spout back into its sleeve.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00; 1,505,900 US jobs): "Measure and record food and liquid intake or urinary and fecal output, reporting changes to medical or nursing staff." LPNs (29-2061.00; 666,900): "Record food and fluid intake and output." For a patient with a Foley catheter this means emptying the drainage bag into a graduate, at least every shift or when half full; 15-25 % of hospital patients may get one (CDC). It is a graded nurse-aide exam skill (Arizona checklist): barrier under the bag, graduate on it, open the drain, empty it completely, "Avoids touching the graduate with any part of the tubing", close the drain, wipe it, put it back in its holder. CDC's CAUTI guideline (III.B.3): a clean container per patient, no splashing, the spigot never touching it. The difficulty is physical: one hand holds a spout on soft tubing a few cm over the mouth, follows the stream as its arc shortens, then pushes the spout up into its sleeve; the other twists the valve.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the floor of an Oatey 34169 plastic washing machine pan (28 x 30 in inside, 29.75 x 31.75 in outside, 2.5 in deep; its near right outside corner at x 6.5, y -42) that stands on the table under the whole scene; its floor stands in for the floor beside the bed, and it catches the water of a failed trial. Catheter bag floor holder (50 cm tall, 21 cm deep, plastic-coated metal), its base fixed at x 45, y -4; hook 48 cm up at x 42. Bard 154002 2000 mL urinary drainage bag (twist-valve drain tube) hanging on it by its hanger, front toward the robot: 18 cm wide, 4.5 cm thick, 25 cm tall, bottom 21 cm up, holding 600 mL of clear tap water standing in for urine (in the sim and the real trial: hygienic and the same every trial). Its drain tube (9 mm across, clear PVC) leaves the bottom's middle, runs out 8.5 cm toward the robot and folds up 11 cm in front of the bag; the twist-valve collar at its end (22 mm long, 12 mm across), with the spout past it (15 mm long, 8 mm across), closed, is pushed fully home in the bag's drain-spout sleeve on a tab in front of the bag. The sleeve is 30 mm deep from its mouth to its closed top, its bore 13 mm across (1 mm wider than the collar); fully home, the spout's tip reaches the sleeve's closed top (x 33.5, y -4, 36 cm up) with 15 mm of the 22 mm collar inside and 7 mm showing below the mouth. The graduate, an Eisco CH0357D 1000 mL short-form polypropylene measuring jug with a handle (14.6 cm tall, 12.7 cm across the top, 11.2 cm across the bottom), empty, stands at x 23, y -25.8 beside the underpad, its handle toward the robot's right. A blue absorbent underpad (29 x 46 cm, long side along y) lies flat on the floor under the bag's front centered at x 28.5, y 4.5. The layout is fixed (object_jitter=0). Real trial: the graduate's rim (top edge, pour-spout lip included), inside walls and inside floor carry a thin coat of red cream lipstick for the touch check, its outside and handle bare; the drain tube is bare. Both grippers wear waterproof covers (nitrile finger cots or cut glove fingers, a clear zipper bag over the gripper body taped at the wrist and round the camera), and each forearm a clear bag sleeve.
scoring: In the graduate is the water that reached it; spilled is what landed anywhere else (underpad, pan floor), including a stream that runs into a hand or arm (it splashes off). A touch is real contact: any point of the drain tube's surface (its run out of the bag, the folded-up tube, the valve collar and the spout past it) within 0.5 mm of the graduate's rim (top edge, pour-spout lip included), inside wall or inside floor at any time from the start of the trial to its end, checked every control step and along the motion between steps; a robot link that touched those surfaces and then touches the tube also makes a touch (it carries the lipstick). The outside wall and handle, where the hands carry the graduate, do not count. Score 0 when more than 20 mL is spilled (a puddle on the floor), or when a stream runs into a hand or arm for more than 1 s in all. Otherwise: 1.0 for at least 570 mL in the graduate (95 % of the 600 mL), at most 5 mL spilled, the valve closed (within 10 degrees of its closed stop), the spout fully home in its sleeve (its tip within 4 mm of the sleeve's closed top, with at least 11 mm of the 22 mm collar inside the sleeve, at most 11 mm showing below the mouth, and the collar straight in the bore; fully home is the tip at the top with 15 mm inside and 7 mm showing), the graduate upright (within 10 degrees of vertical) and standing on the underpad, and both hands clear (every tool point and pad tip 1 cm from the spout, the tube and the graduate, and in the sim no part of either arm within 1 cm of the tube, so only the sleeve holds the spout up) with everything still, held 1 s; 0.75 for at least 570 mL with the valve closed and the graduate upright; 0.5 for at least 570 mL otherwise (valve left open, graduate tipped after) or at least 300 mL with the valve closed and the graduate upright; 0.25 for at least 100 mL. A touch at any time caps the trial at 0.25. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. In the sim, if either arm's collision hulls cannot be read at any step, the trial cannot score 1.0. Real trial: the graduate's net mass on a 1 g kitchen scale (1 g = 1 mL); spilled is the pre-weighed underpad's gain plus what is wiped up off the pan floor and the covers with pre-weighed paper towels; a touch is any red on a white paper towel wiped over the whole drain tube, the collar and the spout after the trial; the time a stream runs into a hand or arm is read from the 60 fps side video; valve, spout in its sleeve (a side photo with a ruler against the collar at the sleeve's mouth), graduate upright and on the underpad, and hands clear from the photo and video. The operator stops a trial whose stream runs onto an arm for more than 1 s or whose tube is dropped with the valve open (close the valve, end the trial, score it as it stands).
reset_notes: About 8 minutes. Unhook the bag and drain what is left into the sink; weigh 600 g of clear tap water into the spare graduate on the scale and pour it through a small kitchen funnel into the bag's inlet tube held above the bag; rehang the bag, close the valve and push the spout fully home in its sleeve (7 mm of collar showing below the mouth). Wash the used graduate and the drain tube with dish soap and warm water, rinse and dry them. Coat the dry spare graduate's rim, inside walls and floor thinly with the lipstick and blot it once, tare it and set it on its tape circle with the handle to the right. Lay a fresh pre-weighed underpad on its tape marks. Wipe the pan floor and the covers dry, replace any bag cover with red on it, and fit fresh finger cots.
fidelity: Clear tap water in sim and real trial. Lumped flow model: the pillow bag drains through the spout as an orifice (Torricelli, Cd 0.61, 6 mm bore, times the valve's opening); the stream follows its arc into the mouth, onto the floor, or off an arm it hits; the graduate holds the volume, sloshes and spills if tipped or shaken. Rigid bag on a hook hinge; the tube is two hinged links, damped only; the valve turns against joint friction; the spout's sleeve holds by contact and friction.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (2,050 steps / 102.5 s; the bag emptied into the graduate with no touch, the valve closed, the spout fully home in its sleeve, the graduate on the underpad). Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps). Both on task.py cf11bdaf20c9.
